chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Going to Percy Lee's to find Art Tatum; Reginald Forsythe scoffs
summary: As a teenager he goes to Percy Lee's; composer Reginald Forsythe dismisses Tatum as a parlor player.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Well, how well did you get to know Tatum?
Oh, let's go back to him by all means anyways. So I left you at that party.

And therefore, I said, 'Where are you going to be playing? Where do you hang out?' 'I hang out at a place called Percy Lee's at (?).' 'Okay, I'll be there.' So I said, 'Oh my goodness, I'm going to get close to him.'

Well, when I went up to Percy Lee's, I couldn't get to him. There was a crowd up there already! Different piano players came to see him, watch him play. The way he would take a... He used to like to drink beer; that gave him ...(?)., I guess.
I remember one night there was a composer, General Reginald Forsythe was his name, from...
He was a black guy from England.
He had a (?) called "The Gay Divorcee" and he had some compositions that became very famous here. He came here from England to appear on broadcasts.
He went to Chicago... You know, he arranged "Deep Forest" for Earl Hines, which was his theme.
Yeah, he worked in Chicago with Earl.

I didn't know that. Well, this fellow stood up there and waited. He talked about Art Tatum. He said, "Ah, this is another one of those parlor social players" or something... Anyway, he wasn't very kind in what he was saying. He just thought he was an ordinary chooka-chooka piano player, you know. He was very proper. He had his handkerchief in his... Very English. So we all winked, you
